Detrending experiments (sector 1)

Each version of the search scored on sector 1's three samples. Variant 7a, a cubic spline whose knot spacing is chosen for each star, found more planets than the running median and roughly halved the signals on stars with no SPOC detection. Variant 7c first removes stellar variability faster than 1.5 days, only on stars that vary that fast; over sectors 1-13 it found 682 of 707 planets against 7a's 676. The TCEs it no longer finds are short-period variability that never became TOIs. Variant 7d, the current default, removes up to ten periodicities instead of three, down to 15-minute periods: the same 682 planets, and on pulsating stars 58% of strong injected transits found against 48%. TCE counts are those in the search's period range.

Planets SPOC found in the same sector that the search still misses

Forced SNR is the transit measured at its known ephemeris on the search's own detrended flux. Below about 7, the transit is too weak in that flux for the search to find; "weak after detrend" means SPOC detected it in this sector, so the loss is the search's.

Sectors 1–13 stitched together

Stars observed in at least 9 of sectors 1–13 were also searched once over the whole year: each sector flattened as above, the sectors joined and binned to 10 minutes, then searched from 1 day to half the baseline (about 180 days). A planet then needs two transits in the year rather than two in one ~27-day sector. Across the samples with TCE stars it found — of — planets and candidates in its period range, — of them with periods longer than a sector, which no single-sector search can find (the longest — days).

⚠️ Its false-alarm rate is high. Each sample was also searched with every light curve turned upside down, where no real transit survives, so every signal found there is a false alarm. With the adopted settings — of — such stars (—%, 95% interval —–—%) gave a signal; as observed, — of — stars with no TCE did (—%), a similar rate. So a stitched signal on a star SPOC made no TCE for is unvetted and most likely a false alarm. Three further tests, each fixed before a fresh sample was run (rejecting edges of data gaps, requiring the dips not to look the same upside down, and rejecting stellar variability at a harmonic of the period), all left more than 6% of upside-down stars with a signal and were not adopted; their samples are shown as run.

Terms

TCE
Threshold Crossing Event: a periodic dip SPOC's search found in one sector. A detection, not a planet; many are eclipsing binaries or systematics.
TOI
TESS Object of Interest: a detection human vetters promoted to a candidate, often using several sectors. Dispositions: CP confirmed planet, KP known planet, PC planet candidate, EB eclipsing binary, V variable star, IS instrumental.
Found again
The search reports a signal at the same period (or a simple multiple or fraction of it) whose transits fall at the same times.
Too weak in one sector
Fewer than two transits in the sector, or the transit measured at its known ephemeris on the search's flux is below the detection threshold. Such a TOI was found with more data than one sector.
SDE
Signal detection efficiency: how far the best peak of the search stands above the other trial periods, in standard deviations. The stitched search tries about 15 times as many periods as one sector, so it requires SDE 13 where one sector requires 11.
Upside down
The same light curve with brightness inverted about its mean. A real transit becomes a brightening, which the search ignores, so every signal found on an inverted curve is a false alarm: a direct measure of the false-alarm rate on that kind of star.
Stitched samples
Drawn at random from the stars with 2-minute data in at least 9 of sectors 1–13, each sharing no star with the samples before it. A and B were run with the adopted settings after those settings were fixed; C and D each tested one extra veto, with its pass conditions written down before the run. Samples A, C and D hold 150 stars with SPOC TCEs and 50 or 250 without; B holds 250 without.
Samples
TOI sample: every TOI listing the sector, on a star with a 2-minute light curve there. TCE samples: 60 stars with TCEs, spread across SPOC's signal strength, plus 40 random stars with none. Sector 1 has two (development and a hold-out sharing no star with it); sector 2 has one, run after all tuning was done on sector 1.

Produced by the fwh_tess search (a Python pilot, not an FFL workflow) from TESS 2-minute light curves read from MAST's public archive, compared with SPOC's single-sector TCE tables and the TOI catalogue. Data snapshot: 2026-11-09.
